title: Crime and Peter Chambers
paragraphs: A hard-boiled detective series based on Henry Kane's private eye Peter Chambers, following the New York investigator through murder cases and underworld entanglements.

NBC sustaining private-detective series based on Henry Kane’s pre-existing Peter Chambers character. Twenty-three broadcasts aired; the frozen GRH set contains all 21 known surviving broadcasts plus four non-broadcast OTRR/GRH reference tracks. Historical numbering preserves missing programs #8 (May 25) and #10 (June 8) rather than compressing the sequence.
GRH documents the program through 23-broadcast NBC run (April 6, 1954 to September 7, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|dane-clark|Dane Clark]] (performer on 21 recordings), Fred Collins (announcer on 21 recordings), Fred Weihe (director on 21 recordings and transcriber on 2 recordings), Henry Kane (producer on 21 recordings, writer on 21 recordings, and creator on 20 recordings), William Zuckert (performer on 19 recordings), Donald Buka (performer on 3 recordings), and Lesley Woods (performer on 3 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include private detective investigation, New York City crime and nightlife, murder and suspicious death, private detective and police cooperation, clubs, ballrooms and entertainment venues, and embezzlement, inheritance and financial motive.

A hard-boiled detective series based on Henry Kane's private eye Peter Chambers, following the New York investigator through murder cases and underworld entanglements.

NBC sustaining private-detective series based on Henry Kane’s pre-existing Peter Chambers character. Twenty-three broadcasts aired; the frozen GRH set contains all 21 known surviving broadcasts plus four non-broadcast OTRR/GRH reference tracks. Historical numbering preserves missing programs #8 (May 25) and #10 (June 8) rather than compressing the sequence.

GRH documents the program through 23-broadcast NBC run (April 6, 1954 to September 7, 1954) on NBC Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Dane Clark (performer on 21 recordings), Fred Collins (announcer on 21 recordings), Fred Weihe (director on 21 recordings and transcriber on 2 recordings), Henry Kane (producer on 21 recordings, writer on 21 recordings, and creator on 20 recordings), William Zuckert (performer on 19 recordings), Donald Buka (performer on 3 recordings), and Lesley Woods (performer on 3 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to NBC Radio Network (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include private detective investigation, New York City crime and nightlife, murder and suspicious death, private detective and police cooperation, clubs, ballrooms and entertainment venues, and embezzlement, inheritance and financial motive.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Henry Kane brings his literary detective to radio, 1954 NBC sustaining private-eye series, 23 broadcasts, 21 surviving, and OTRR/GRH reference material in archive container.
